title: Maratha Empire
summary: The Maratha state began with Shivaji, who took the royal title Chhatrapati in 1674 in the hill country of the western Deccan. Under his grandson Shahu the office of Peshwa, based at Pune, became the hereditary head of a loose confederacy of Maratha rulers. Through the 1700s the Marathas seized Mughal lands in western and southern India becoming perhaps the most formidable military power in India, though defeat at Panipat in 1761 badly weakened them. Three wars with the East India Company ended the confederacy in 1818.

uncertainty.note: Begins with Shivaji's coronation in 1674; ends with the defeat of Peshwa Baji Rao II in the Third Anglo-Maratha War in 1818.

as_recorded.value: Maratha Confederacy of India (aka the Mahrattas, 1674-1818)

where.historical_name: Pune, capital and seat of the Peshwas of the Maratha Confederacy

importance.justification: Displaced Mughal power across much of India in the 18th century before the British conquest (R3 D3 T2 L3).
